$description: Portfolio design tokens, DTCG source of truth. Generated artifact is tokens.css (symlinked into the portfolio + case studies). Three tiers: primitives (hue+stop ramps) feed semantics (role), and component tokens (btn/card/chip/badge) alias semantics, never primitives. Faithful v1 transcription of the hand-written tokens.css; naming aliases + $type annotations layered in a later stage.

0.$description: Card surface; text on an accent fill.

150.$description: Half-step. accent-subtle on light; text-primary on dark.

700.$description: Text-secondary on light; strong border on dark.

850.$description: Half-step. Brand ink; accent on light; surface on dark.

950.$description: bg on dark; text-primary on light; accent-hover on light.

400.$description: Lime tint, one step under the brand value.

500.$description: Brand lime. The single canonical lime, the only stop consumed as identity (--brand-primary).

me.natemills.usage.role: The single canonical brand identity lime (--brand-primary).
me.natemills.usage.use: Brand identity only: primary button fill, brand outlines, focus rings on dark surfaces, the lime period and active dot.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never as body text or links on a light background (1.06:1 on --color-bg, computed 2026-06-10, fails WCAG AA), and never as a theme-aware accent; the theme-aware role is color.accent, not this fixed identity value.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Fixed brand identity value (audit TK-05); other lime stops are supporting tints, not identity.

550.$description: Saturated vivid lime; the highest-chroma stop (OKLCH chroma 0.229), sitting between 500 and 600 in lightness.

600.$description: Hover-dim lime, one step darker than brand identity; the target of --brand-primary-dim.

900.$description: Darkest usable lime, a near-black shade.

400.$description: Yellow tint, one step under the secondary value.

500.$description: Brand yellow, the house secondary (--brand-secondary): the colour the brand gradient runs into from lime.

me.natemills.usage.role: The house secondary brand colour (--brand-secondary), the yellow lime runs into in the brand gradient.
me.natemills.usage.use: Brand gradients and the Kind words and footer grounds, beside lime. It is what --brand-primary-vivid and --brand-spot resolve to on the live site.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never as text or links on a light background (it is lighter than lime, which already fails there), and never as a theme-aware accent.
me.natemills.usage.decision: A primitive ramp, not a one-off, so the design-system view shows two brand sets, Primary and Secondary, like every Theme lab preset now does.

550.$description: Saturated vivid yellow, sitting between 500 and 600 in lightness.

600.$description: Dim yellow, one step darker than the secondary value.

900.$description: Darkest usable yellow, a near-black shade.

yellow.$description: The house SECONDARY ramp, lime's partner (Nathan, 2026-09-24). Derived from the lime ramp rather than hand-picked: every stop keeps lime's lightness step, re-anchored so 500 is the shipped brand yellow, with lime's chroma profile and hue drift; the hex is the sRGB-mapped value. Primitives: components read the brand.* and color.* roles, never these directly.

me.natemills.usage.role: The bare space-separated RGB channel triplet behind --brand-primary (210 255 55). A fragment of a colour function, not a colour value.
me.natemills.usage.use: Only inside modern slash syntax for lime at an alpha: rgb(var(--brand-primary-rgb) / 0.2). Faint washes, glow shadows, alpha borders.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never as a colour on its own (color, background, border-color, fill) and never in the legacy comma form rgba(var(--brand-primary-rgb), 0.2). The emitted value is the bare triplet, so both are invalid at computed-value time and the declaration is silently dropped with nothing in the console. Most design systems ship a comma-separated -rgb triplet, so the reflex form is the wrong one here. For solid lime use brand.primary.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Governed as a pair with brand.ink-rgb: these are the only two channel tokens in the system, and half-covering the class would imply the other is safe.

primary-rgb.$description: Channel form of --brand-primary for decorative alpha shadows: rgb(var(--brand-primary-rgb) / 0.2). DERIVED by build.mjs from the referenced colour's hex anchor (audit TK-05), never hand-typed.

primary-dim.$description: Hover-dim step of the brand lime (lime.600).

primary-vivid.$description: The hot vivid-yellow end of brand.gradient: yellow.500, the house secondary (#eeff00; a raw value until the yellow ramp existed, 2026-09-24). Gradient stop only. Renamed from --brand-emphasis-2 (2026-07-02; the dangling -2 had no -1).

secondary.$description: The second brand colour, lime's partner: the yellow the brand gradient runs into. The Theme lab repaints it per preset from the preset's heading colour (Rave keeps its authored hot pink), so a theme's Secondary set is the second colour you actually see on its page (Nathan, 2026-09-24).

spot.$description: The far end of brand.gradient, addressable on its own. Identical to brand.primary-vivid on the live site; it exists because the Kind words and footer grounds need that second stop as a COLOUR rather than as part of a gradient string. Under a Theme lab preset it is the preset's primary nudged by the house step, the same small move lime makes to yellow, so the grounds stay one family instead of clashing (Nathan, 2026-09-24); Rave keeps its authored pink. brand.gradient reads it, so a re-point moves both.

ink.$description: Fixed, theme-invariant brand ink. The always-dark bed, and the dark foreground on a fixed lime or static-white bed.

me.natemills.usage.role: Fixed, theme-invariant brand ink (neutral.850). Both the always-dark bed and the dark foreground used on fixed lime or fixed light beds.
me.natemills.usage.use: Always-dark surfaces that must not flip (card.dark-bg, the about showreel frame) and the dark foreground or pinned focus ring on a fixed lime or static-white bed (btn.primary-fg on btn.primary-bg, the footer icon buttons).
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never leave a theme-aware token on it. In the DEFAULT light theme color.focus-ring, color.accent, color.accent-emphasis, color.link and color.border-hover all resolve to this same neutral.850, so each paints 1.00:1 on an ink bed; in the DEFAULT dark theme color.surface resolves to it too, so ink text or borders on a normal card are equally invisible. On an always-dark bed pin the focus ring to brand.primary (14.65:1 on ink) and take text from the color.on-ink-* family.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Fixed identity value: never give brand.ink a per-theme override. Governs the fixed-bed half of the theme trap; color.on-accent governs the foreground half.

me.natemills.usage.role: The bare space-separated RGB channel triplet behind --brand-ink (28 28 31). A fragment of a colour function, not a colour value.
me.natemills.usage.use: Only inside modern slash syntax to get ink at an alpha: rgb(var(--brand-ink-rgb) / 0.55). That is how every live consumer reads it: scrims, glass tints, soft shadows, muted emphasis text.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never as a colour on its own (color, background, border-color, fill) and never in the legacy comma form rgba(var(--brand-ink-rgb), 0.55). The emitted value is the bare triplet, so both are invalid at computed-value time and the property silently falls back to inherited or initial with nothing in the console. For a plain ink colour use brand.ink.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Governed as a pair with brand.primary-rgb: these are the only two channel tokens in the system, and half-covering the class would imply the other is safe.

ink-rgb.$description: Channel form of --brand-ink for ink-at-alpha: rgb(var(--brand-ink-rgb) / 0.65). DERIVED by build.mjs from the referenced colour's hex anchor (audit TK-05).

gradient.$description: CSS-only composite; reads var(--brand-primary) and var(--brand-spot) so the gradient follows a brand re-point at CSS level (audit TK-05; DTCG forbids embedded aliases inside string values, review 2026-06-10). The explicit 'in oklab' preserves the perceptual midpoint the gradient had when its stops were oklch(): rgb()/hex stops interpolate in sRGB by default, which would shift the blend by up to 11/255 (sRGB emission switch, 2026-07-27).

anthropic-large.$description: Anthropic orange, 18px+ bold. EXTERNAL brand: a locked, theme-agnostic constant, never aliased into a semantic token, not part of our palette.

anthropic-body.$description: Anthropic orange, darker 12-14px variant for contrast. External brand: locked constant.

linkedin.$description: LinkedIn brand blue, the LinkedIn mark only. External brand: locked constant.

bupa-blue.$description: Bupa brand blue, Bupa case-study context only. External brand: locked constant.

bupa-blue-dark.$description: Bupa brand blue, darker variant. External brand: locked constant.

bupa-blue-subtle.$description: Bupa brand blue, subtle tint. External brand: locked constant.

github.$description: GitHub brand near-black, the GitHub mark only. External brand: locked constant.

wcag-amber.$description: W3C WCAG conformance badge amber, that badge only. External brand: locked constant.

glitch-magenta.$description: Decorative glitch effect only. Not a palette colour, never themed.

glitch-cyan.$description: Decorative glitch effect only. Not a palette colour, never themed.

burst.$description: How long one glitch burst lasts. The scramble runs for exactly this long, then the echo goes back to nothing.

shift.$description: Resting separation of the two colour copies either side of the emphasis word.

strength.$description: Opacity of each colour copy at full burst. Held flat for the whole burst so the echo moves without pulsing, which is what keeps it clear of the three-flash rule.

bg.$description: The page canvas. Brand off-white in light, near-black in dark.

surface.$description: The default card / panel surface. White card on the grey page in light (a genuine lift); the lighter near-black (#1c1c1f) in dark.

surface-sunken.$description: Recessed wells, insets, thumbnails, chips. A step below the card surface: light grey in light; the darker near-black (#141416) in dark.

surface-inverse.$description: A slab that stays near-black in both themes, like the testimonials band.

me.natemills.usage.role: Theme-invariant always-dark slab surface (near-black).
me.natemills.usage.use: Full-bleed inverse bands that must stay near-black in BOTH themes, e.g. the testimonials section and the matching metrics band.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Do not use as a normal card or panel surface (that is color.surface), and never add a per-theme override; it is intentionally not theme-reactive, like static-white in reverse.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Theme-invariant by design: resolves to the darkest stop in every theme so the inverse band reads identically. Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Always-dark slab surface, theme-invariant near-black (#0a0a0b). The full-bleed testimonials section stays near-black in BOTH themes (the metrics band matches it via a local theme scope); never overridden per theme, like static-white in reverse.

surface-inverse-sunken.$description: An inset panel on an always-dark slab. The same value in both themes.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Inset on an inverse slab, theme-invariant near-black (#141416), the same dark value as surface-sunken. The testimonial portrait image-load fallback; never overridden per theme. Reads lighter than surface-inverse because neutral.950 is the darkest stop in the scale.

text-primary.$description: Default reading text. Near-black on light, near-white on dark.

text-secondary.$description: Secondary text: supporting copy one step quieter than text-primary.

text-tertiary.$description: Tertiary text: section labels and quiet meta copy; the last step that still clears 4.5:1 on light.

border.$description: Default hairline border and divider colour, theme-aware.

border-strong.$description: Heavier border for edges that must read past a hairline (secondary-button outlines).

border-brand.$description: The brand-lime outline accent (active selection, link underline, brand ring). Theme-invariant lime, never overridden per theme; the semantic the brand outlines read instead of the raw primitive.

border-hover.$description: Border colour on hover: ink on light, lime on dark.

accent.$description: The single theme-aware interactive role: ink on light, brand lime on dark. Active and selected states.

me.natemills.usage.role: The theme-aware accent role: ink (neutral.850) on light, brand lime on dark.
me.natemills.usage.use: Anywhere the accent should follow the theme, e.g. the active carousel dot and accent surfaces.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Do not assume this is lime or hardcode lime here; on the light page it is ink and only flips to lime on dark. For the fixed brand lime use brand.primary / lime.500.

accent-hover.$description: Hover step of the accent role.

accent-subtle.$description: Quiet accent wash for subtle active or highlighted surfaces.

me.natemills.usage.role: The theme-following contrast pair of color.accent: pure white (neutral.0) on light, near-black (neutral.950) on dark.
me.natemills.usage.use: Text and icons on a fill painted with color.accent, so the foreground flips with the theme alongside its background (the Under-the-Hood colour-card gallery, the list toggle in its pressed state).
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never as the foreground on a fill that stays brand lime in BOTH themes, such as the primary button or the lime footer slab. On light this token is pure white, and white on brand lime is 1.16:1. Those surfaces pair with brand.on-primary or btn.primary-fg (ink, 14.65:1 on lime). A foreground may only flip with the theme when its background flips too, and axe does not evaluate icon contrast, so the icon case ships silently.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Governs the foreground half of the theme trap; brand.ink governs the fixed-bed half. Do not assume on-accent means on-primary.

on-accent.$description: Text or icons sitting on an accent fill; the contrast pair of color.accent. Renamed from --color-accent-foreground (2026-07-02) to join the on-* family.

focus-ring.$description: Theme-aware keyboard-focus colour: ink on light, lime on dark. Consumed via border.focus.

me.natemills.usage.role: Theme-aware keyboard-focus colour: ink on light, lime on dark.
me.natemills.usage.use: The focus indicator colour, consumed via border.focus.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Do not hardcode a single colour and do not remove it without a replacement focus style; it must flip per theme to stay visible.

link.$description: Underlined navigational link text: ink on light, lime on dark. Distinct role from accent (Section 10).

on-ink-emphasis.$description: Solid-white emphasis step of the on-ink family (full white, above the 88% on-ink-primary); theme-invariant. Reserved for full-white emphasis on always-dark slabs; currently unconsumed outside the Under-the-Hood gallery (the hero headline moved to --color-text-primary with the 2026-06-25 editorial hero). Renamed from --color-hero-text-primary (2026-07-02; a component name squatting in the semantic namespace).

on-ink-strong.$description: Near-white text on an always-dark slab (neutral.50). The second loudest step of the on-ink family, one notch below on-ink-emphasis and above on-ink-primary. Theme-invariant, never on a light surface. Used for dark-section titles and hover text on inverse bands.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Renamed twice. It was --color-neutral-subtle until 2026-07-07 (a surface-family name on a text role), which fixed the object half and kept the prominence half. Renamed again 2026-08-26 from on-ink-subtle to on-ink-strong: at 98% white it is the second brightest of the seven, so a word meaning quiet was naming the second loudest colour, and its own description called it both 'the softest step' and 'a hair below emphasis' in one sentence. 'strong' is an existing house prominence word rather than a new one, and it sorts with the values.

on-ink-primary.$description: Primary text on an always-dark slab (88% white).

me.natemills.usage.role: Primary text colour for content sitting on an always-dark slab (88% white).
me.natemills.usage.use: Headings and body text on an ink or dark band.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never on a light surface; it is white-on-dark only and will vanish on a white card. For text on light use color.text-primary.

on-ink-secondary.$description: Secondary text on an always-dark slab (66% white).

me.natemills.usage.role: Secondary text colour for content on an always-dark slab (66% white).
me.natemills.usage.use: Muted or secondary copy on an ink or dark band.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never on a light surface; white-on-dark only. For muted text on light use color.text-secondary.

on-ink-muted.$description: Quiet fills and inactive dots on an always-dark slab. Not a text colour.

me.natemills.usage.role: Muted NON-TEXT step of the on-ink family (40% white).
me.natemills.usage.use: Inactive dots, quiet fills and pressed-state washes on an ink or dark band.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never as small body text: it composites to 3.77:1 over color.surface-inverse, below the 4.5:1 small-text floor. For muted TEXT on a dark slab use color.on-ink-secondary (8.00:1). Never on a light surface.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Contrast-gated to non-text use, the same gate color.text-muted-emphasis carries at ~3.7:1 (audit 2026-07-25 #14). Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Muted NON-TEXT step of the on-ink family (40% white): inactive dots, quiet fills and pressed-state washes on an always-dark slab. Composites to 3.77:1 over color.surface-inverse, 3.83:1 over surface-inverse-sunken and 3.79:1 over brand-ink, so it clears the SC 1.4.11 3:1 non-text floor but fails the SC 1.4.3 4.5:1 small-text floor. Not a body-text colour, despite the on-ink family name.

on-ink-border.$description: Hairline border on an always-dark slab (8% white).

static-white.$description: Theme-invariant white, never overridden per theme.

static-white-hover.$description: Hover step for static-white surfaces; theme-invariant light grey.

accent-emphasis.$description: Theme-aware emphasis text following the accent role: ink on light, lime on dark. For text on theme-following surfaces; on-* tokens are for fixed-colour surfaces. Renamed from --color-brand-emphasis (2026-07-02; one interactive role, accent).

dot-inactive.$description: The unfilled half of the carousel position indicator. NAME WARNING: it still says dot, but there are no pagination dots on the site; .ds-dots was deleted 2026-07-12 and the one carousel control is .ds-carousel-nav, a rail. Renaming the pair is a follow-up (it moves the showcase manifest and the doc tables too), so the job is written here instead. No CSS reads this token today: .ds-carousel-nav__rail paints its groove from --cn-rail-track, which defaults to --color-border. It is kept as the tuned partner of --color-dot-active, and the theme lab repaints the pair together. Solid theme-aware grey: clears the SC 1.4.11 3:1 floor on light surfaces (the old rgba(127,127,127,0.45) composited to 1.67:1); dark themes override to neutral-500.

me.natemills.usage.role: The unfilled half of the carousel position indicator; a solid theme-aware grey tuned for contrast.
me.natemills.usage.use: The unfilled half of a carousel position indicator on standard surfaces. Not pagination dots: the site has none.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Do not substitute a translucent grey: the old rgba(127,127,127,0.45) was only 1.67:1. Inverse bands restyle the carousel nav via --cn-rail-fill/--cn-rail-track, not by re-scoping this token.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Tuned to clear the SC 1.4.11 3:1 non-text contrast floor.

dot-active.$description: The fill on the carousel nav progress rail (.ds-carousel-nav__fill), reached through --cn-rail-fill, which defaults to this token. NAME WARNING: it still says dot, but there are no pagination dots on the site; .ds-dots was deleted 2026-07-12 and the rail replaced it. Renaming the pair is a follow-up (it moves the showcase manifest and the doc tables too), so the job is written here instead. Follows the accent: ink on light, lime on dark (lime on the light page was 1.06:1, audit AX-01). A band restyles the nav by re-mapping --cn-rail-fill/--cn-rail-track locally, never this token.

me.natemills.usage.role: Muted italic emphasis text.
me.natemills.usage.use: Emphasis words inside headings and muted lists; any size, light surfaces.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Do not re-add an alpha value here: the 55% ink version composited to ~3.7:1 on light and passed or failed depending on the backdrop (W55). The dark theme flips this to brand-lime, so never lean on it for text that also renders on light fixed surfaces.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Went solid in the W55 alpha consolidation (2026-08-11); was rgb(var(--brand-ink-rgb) / 0.55), audits TK-07 and C-01.

text-muted-emphasis.$description: C-01 muted italic emphasis. Solid neutral-600 on light (clears the 4.5:1 small-text floor on every light surface), flips to brand-lime on dark. Was 55% ink alpha until W55 (2026-08-11): the alpha composited to ~3.7:1 on light (audit TK-07). Renamed from --color-text-muted-em (2026-07-02; em read as the CSS unit).

on-ink-hover.$description: C-12 hover/focus tint on dark backgrounds.

on-primary-strong.$description: Strong text on the brand-lime slab: the exact solid composite of 78% ink over brand.primary, baked in W55 (2026-08-11) so footer text stays one colour while the image trail transits behind it. 7.67:1 on brand.primary. Theme-invariant, the lime slab does not flip. Follows the Material on-<surface> convention (on-primary, on-surface); pairs with color.on-primary-muted.

me.natemills.usage.role: Strong body and label text on the fixed brand-lime slab (footer, lime bento tiles).
me.natemills.usage.use: Eyebrows, body copy and labels sitting directly on brand.primary.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never on any surface other than brand-lime; it is a baked composite and carries no meaning elsewhere. Do not replace with translucent ink: the footer image trail passes behind this text.
me.natemills.usage.decision: W55 alpha consolidation (2026-08-11): was rgb(var(--brand-ink-rgb) / 0.78) at 6 sites.

on-primary-muted.$description: Muted text on the brand-lime slab: the exact solid composite of 68% ink over brand.primary, baked in W55 (2026-08-11). 5.51:1 on brand.primary, clearing the 4.5:1 small-text floor the footer closer was hand-tuned for. Theme-invariant; pairs with color.on-primary-strong.

me.natemills.usage.role: Muted small text on the fixed brand-lime slab (footer closer, quiet meta rows).
me.natemills.usage.use: Small secondary copy sitting directly on brand.primary.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never on any surface other than brand-lime. Do not dim further: 0.6 ink alpha composited under the 4.5:1 floor, which is why the closer sat at 0.68.
me.natemills.usage.decision: W55 alpha consolidation (2026-08-11): absorbs the 0.65 to 0.7 ink-on-lime cluster.

feedback-background-error.$description: Error message backgrounds: deep red on light, soft red on dark.

me.natemills.usage.role: Error-state fill: a surface that says something is failing.
me.natemills.usage.use: Small error chips and fills, paired with color.on-feedback-error as the ink.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never as text on its own, and never for emphasis that is not an actual failure state. Do not pair with any foreground other than color.on-feedback-error.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: The error fill of the feedback family: deep red on light, soft red on dark. Its first consumer, the theme lab's contrast FAIL chip, retired with the 2026-09-01 lab uplift, so the pair currently waits for its next error surface; it stays because it is the Section 16 naming example made real. Named per the Section 16 order (object-property-variant); no red primitive ramp exists yet because two values do not clear the rule of three, so the values live here with this ruling.

on-feedback-error.$description: Contrast pair for content sitting on feedback-background-error: white on the deep light-theme red, near-black red on the soft dark-theme red. 8.7:1 light, 8.9:1 dark.

me.natemills.usage.role: Ink on the error fill.
me.natemills.usage.use: Text and icons sitting directly on color.feedback-background-error.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never on any other surface; on the page grounds it is just white or dark red with no meaning.

overlay-soft.$description: Soft scrim behind floating chrome (35% black).

overlay-base.$description: Standard modal and lightbox scrim (62% black).

overlay-strong.$description: Heavy scrim for maximum content isolation (88% black).

display.$description: Display headings and large numbers. Anton, one weight, never faux-bolded.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Display headings (h1 to h6) and large numbers. Anton ships a single 400 weight, so font-synthesis-weight is switched off site-wide; asking for 800 gets the real drawn 400, not a browser-faked bold.

mono.$value: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace
mono.$description: Tabular numbers, code, and eyebrow labels.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Absorbed the --font-mono-metric alias on 2026-07-02: the alias carried an identical stack, and the IBM Plex Mono drift it once guarded against is recorded in Section 4 history.

feature-mono.$description: Switches on the slashed zero for every piece of mono text.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: OpenType slashed-zero feature for ALL mono text, applied once at :root in portfolio/assets/fonts.css rather than per rule. Requires the self-hosted full JetBrains Mono release: the Google Fonts build subsets the `zero` feature out, which left this token inert from the day it was written until the 2026-08-20 self-host. Never let a component override font-feature-settings; that silently restores the dotted zero.

xs.$description: 12px. Captions, footnotes, fine print; --text-caption resolves here.

sm.$description: 14px. Compact body: footer text, card bullets, dense UI copy.

lg.$description: 18px. Intro lines, award titles, component names.

2xl.$description: 32px. Small display headings; today only the type-scale specimen consumes it directly.

3xl.$description: 48px. The largest fixed stop; the fluid display clamps take over above it.

h1.$description: The base display size every other heading size is derived from.

me.natemills.usage.role: The base display curve that heading sizes derive from; section h2s themselves run on display.section (1.5x this).
me.natemills.usage.use: Derived heading sizes (the About heading at 1.25x, the Experience company names at 0.75x).
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Do not use for the hero headline; the hero is a documented exception with its own mobile-tuned clamp (use display.hero).
me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: The base display curve. Section h2s run on display.section (1.5x this); the About heading and the Experience company names derive from it via documented multipliers in sections.css. The hero h1 is a documented exception with its own mobile-tuned clamp.

h2.$description: Card titles, intro lines, sub-headings inside section bodies.

body.$description: Paragraphs, lists, default reading text, card body copy.

label.$description: Uppercase mono labels, eyebrows, stat labels, badges.

meta.$description: 13px meta tier, between caption (12px) and compact body (14px).

nav.$description: Header menu links. Body font, sentence case, 14px.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Diverged from text.label on 2026-08-21. The nav had been set in the eyebrow voice (mono, uppercase, 11px, wide tracking), a label style doing a wayfinding job, which left it the quietest text on the page. The token was always held separate from text.label so this change would not touch every eyebrow.

hero.$description: Display type at hero scale, fluid 40 to 118px. This site’s own hero headline is a documented exception: it sets its own clamps and runs larger still.

me.natemills.usage.role: Display-scale size at hero proportions. Its one consumer is the Under-the-Hood display specimen.
me.natemills.usage.use: The Under-the-Hood display specimen (uth.html). Any new surface wanting hero-scale display type.

fg.$description: Badge label and icon colour; quiet by design, auto-flips per theme.

border.$description: Badge outline; hairline, auto-flips per theme.

radius.$description: Circle geometry: dots, markers, slider thumbs, and drawn circles (the brand period, status dots, touch-target rings). Portraits moved to avatar.radius on 2026-09-02. Full by definition: a re-theme that softens buttons leaves a dot round, and the theme lab's corner tier squares it only when the whole system goes sharp (0 at sharp, full at soft and round). Exists so component rules stop reading radius.full directly (the Section 16 red flag).

End-cap rounding for thin bars, rails, tracks, indicators, and capsule strips (progress rails, tab indicators, slider tracks, chart bars, the hero edge widget's pill). Full by definition; it rounds the ends of a strip at any height. The theme lab's corner tier drives it since 2026-09-02 (0 at sharp, 12px at soft, full at round): a strip keeps round ends through soft and squares only when the whole system goes sharp. Exists so component rules stop reading radius.full directly (the Section 16 red flag).

Identity shape: the header profile mark (.avatar / .profile-mark), the Kind words faces (.kw-face) and the hero widget's four theme marks. Full by default, which on a square box is the same circle those surfaces drew with 50% before (2026-09-02). Unlike dot and bar, a corner re-theme MAY drive this one: the round icon buttons beside the portrait already follow --btn-radius, and a portrait that holds its circle next to a squared button reads as the odd one out. The theme lab writes 50% / 25% / 0 for round / soft / sharp, in percentages because the marks render at 18px to 48px and a fixed px would clamp to a circle on the small ones.

section-head-gap.$description: Section rhythm. The single gap from a section heading to the first content under it, owned by .section-head. Fluid because --display-section is itself clamp(51px, 8.7vw, 108px): a fixed gap reads 0.63x the heading at 390px and 0.30x at 1440px, so the rhythm drifts even though the number does not. This holds 0.40x to 0.47x at every width. Same construction as --section-padding.

compact.$description: Compact card-padding tier (16px). Dense content tiles: credential cards, health-check tiles, inner controls.

standard.$description: Standard card-padding tier (24px). The default content-card inset; matches the base .card. The standard, resolving the old 16-vs-24 doc conflict.

spacious.$description: Spacious card-padding tier (32px). Large feature, award, and full-testimonial cards (often the desktop step up from standard).

fast.$description: Hover, focus, and micro state feedback.

stagger.$description: The gap between one item's entrance and the next in a group.

me.natemills.usage.role: The step between siblings in a grouped entrance on a time-based timeline.
me.natemills.usage.use: As animation-delay arithmetic against the item's --i index, on top of the group's own lead, which is itself a multiple of this token so the whole choreography collapses with one value: `animation-delay: calc(var(--duration-stagger) * 5 + var(--i) * var(--duration-stagger))`. Pair it with animation-fill-mode: backwards.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never with animation-fill-mode: both. `both` holds the animation's end frame forever, so an entrance that finishes on transform:none permanently overrides any hover or selected transform on the same element; the theme lab swatch hover grow died silently that way (2026-09-07), and the awards spec rows were carrying the same `both` as a latent landmine until they folded in here. Never as an animation-duration, and never on a scroll-driven timeline, where animation-delay is ignored with nothing in the console.
me.natemills.usage.decision: 24ms, picked by Nathan from a Relaxed/Tight dial on the entrance study (_mockups/tl-entrance) against the real card. The 16ms tight setting saved 120ms across twelve items, which he could not perceive, and cost the stagger its legibility: below roughly 20ms a twelve-item deal reads as one soft simultaneous arrival rather than a deal. Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Stagger tier: the gap between one item's entrance and the next when a group deals in on a normal timeline. NOT a duration a thing runs for, a step between siblings, which is why it is an order of magnitude under fast. Minted 2026-09-07 for the theme lab card, whose twelve swatches had no entrance at all. Second consumer landed 2026-09-07: the awards spec rows, which had a hand-typed --award-text-stagger: 55ms connected to nothing. That was more than double this token, so folding it in was a real change, not a refactor, and the three candidates (keep 55ms, chain 48ms as two steps, adopt the plain 24ms) were built side by side on the real card at _mockups/award-stagger. Nathan could not tell them apart, so the local value was not earning its difference and the exception was dropped rather than documented; the awards sequence now ends at 532ms instead of 625ms, still inside the panel's own 560ms spring. The mobile nav drawer is the third consumer the rule of three counts, and it folded in the same day (sections.css:955): its eight hand-typed nth-child delays became one arithmetic step off this token. For a SCROLL-driven stagger use motion.reveal-stagger instead: animation-delay does nothing on a scroll timeline. Collapsed to 1ms under reduced motion by the block in tokens/build.mjs. That belt is what makes a token-chained stagger honest under reduced motion, since the global rule forces animation-duration but never animation-delay; the awards rows do not rely on it, because the #awards block switches these animations off outright under reduce.

flourish.$description: One playful beat on a small icon: a shake, a roll, a pour.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Flourish tier: one playful beat on a small glyph, a shake, a roll, a slosh, a pour. Sits between slow and expressive because the movement is the message and has to be seen at 16px, yet it is one icon, never a hero moment. Minted 2026-09-06 when the lab dice, the flask and the mail glyph had each typed their own value between 520 and 760ms; add here rather than hand-typing the next one. Collapsed to 1ms under reduced motion by the block in tokens/build.mjs.

beat.$description: The gap between one part of a view's opening and the next.

me.natemills.usage.role: The step between the PARTS of a choreography, one tier above duration.stagger: stagger separates siblings inside a group, this separates the groups themselves (a heading line, the lede, the specimen cards, the resource cards).
me.natemills.usage.use: As animation-delay arithmetic against a sequence index set once in script: `animation-delay: calc(var(--duration-beat) + var(--s) * var(--duration-beat))`, where the leading term is the opening's own pause and is deliberately one beat rather than a separate token. Pair it with animation-fill-mode: backwards.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never as an animation-duration, and never on a scroll-driven timeline, where animation-delay is ignored with nothing in the console. For siblings dealing out inside one group use duration.stagger; for a scroll stagger use motion.reveal-stagger.
me.natemills.usage.decision: 240ms, picked by Nathan from a four-step speed dial on the real page (_mockups/uthmotion, 2026-09-14) after the design-system view's opening read as already finished before he looked at it. The three faster settings were 60, 110 and 170ms; at 240 the whole opening runs about 3.9s and each part is legibly its own moment. Exactly ten steps of duration.stagger, which is the arithmetic relationship, not a coincidence: a group's siblings deal on the small step, the groups themselves land on this one. Minted rather than written as `calc(var(--duration-stagger) * 10)` because a bare multiplier in the stylesheet tells a reader the number but never the intent. First consumer is the design-system view's opening; it is the contract any later view opening adopts.

expressive.$description: The slow, cinematic entrance for one large hero moment.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Expressive tier: the slow, cinematic duration for a single large hero moment (the two-phone Spline scene scales in over this). Deliberately longer than the general-purpose slow tier and reserved for one large-surface entrance, never UI feedback. Collapsed to 1ms under reduced motion by the block in tokens/build.mjs.

marquee.$description: One full lap of a marquee that loops without stopping.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Ambient tier: one full traverse of a continuously looping marquee (the hero pillar ticker). Two orders of magnitude above the expressive tier because it is not a transition, it is a background rhythm nobody is meant to time. The only member of this tier; add here rather than hand-typing a raw duration in the component.

default.$description: The workhorse symmetric curve. Begins and ends on screen.

entrance.$description: Decelerate, for elements entering the screen.

exit.$description: Accelerate, for elements leaving the screen.

emphasized.$description: Pronounced ease-out for overlay and menu entrance motion (items rising into view). A stronger, slower-settling decelerate than --ease-entrance.

spring.$description: Overshoot and settle, so a move reads as a bounce. Micro-moments only.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Overshoot curve: pushes past the target and settles back, so a move reads as a bounce. For playful micro-moments that should feel physical: the dice roll, the flask shake, the shapes glyph, the footer arrow, the award card fold. Never for layout or content transitions, which must land where they are going. Minted 2026-09-06 from three hand-typed copies of the curve (the award card, the footer CTA, the theme lab).

linear.$description: Constant rate, no acceleration. For motion that loops forever.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Constant rate, no acceleration. For continuous loop motion: the hero ticker, both marquees, the glass column scroll, and the loading-icon cycles. Authored as a cubic-bezier twin of the linear keyword so it lives in the ease group with its siblings.

motion.$description: Scroll-reveal entrance geometry AND timing for the native scroll-driven .nm-sr pattern (animation-timeline: view()). The settle curve is {ease.emphasized}. rise/shift/scale/slide are how far a subject travels; begin/settle/stagger are WHEN it travels, expressed as absolute scroll distances so a reveal lands in the same place on screen whatever the subject's height. See design-system.md Section 7.

reveal-rise.$description: translateY start for the signature reveal (settles to 0).

reveal-shift.$description: translateX start that gives the signature reveal its diagonal.

reveal-scale.$description: start scale for the signature reveal (settles to 1).

reveal-slide.$description: translateX start for the slide-from-right reveal: featured + testimonial carousels and the design-system plate illustrations.

reveal-begin.$description: scroll distance after a subject first peeks above the fold before its reveal starts moving.

reveal-settle.$description: scroll distance at which a reveal is fully arrived. Absolute, so a tall card and a short heading both finish with their top the same distance down the screen.

me.natemills.usage.role: The end stop of every scroll reveal's animation-range, measured as a scroll distance from the subject's first contact with the bottom of the screen.
me.natemills.usage.use: As the second stop in animation-range on a view() timeline, always in the entry phase: `animation-range: entry var(--motion-reveal-begin) entry var(--motion-reveal-settle)`. Add the per-item stagger to this stop for grouped items.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never write the end stop as a percentage of the cover range. The cover range is viewport height plus subject height, so a percentage of it lands later the taller the subject and the shorter the screen. That is the defect this token replaced (2026-08-29): measured at 390x844, the awards cards settled with their top 45% down the screen and the testimonial and work bands 22-24% down, most of the way up and still half transparent, while the headings on the same page settled at 59%.
me.natemills.usage.decision: 250px, picked by Nathan from a four-option tuner run on the real page at phone width (option D, Snappy). It lands every band's top 60-67% down the screen, the zone the section headings already occupied and that he had already approved.

reveal-stagger.$description: per-item offset added to the reveal’s end stop so grouped items deal out (animation-delay is ignored on scroll timelines).

me.natemills.usage.role: Per-item offset for the scroll reveal, measured in scroll distance like the begin/settle stops it composes with, not a duration and not a delay.
me.natemills.usage.use: Only in animation-range arithmetic on a scroll-driven timeline, the way .nm-sr does it: multiply by the item's --i index and add to the end stop.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never as animation-delay or transition-delay. animation-delay has no effect on a scroll-driven animation at all, so the stagger silently vanishes with nothing in the console. For a genuine time-based stagger on a normal timeline use the duration.* tokens.
me.natemills.usage.decision: A length, not a percentage. It was 4% until 2026-08-29, when the range stops it composes with became absolute distances; a percentage stagger added to a length stop is invalid arithmetic, and the percentage was itself measured against the height-dependent cover range this token set exists to escape.

none.$description: Square. No rounding, for sharp-cornered surfaces and full-bleed media. Emitted as a bare 0 (identical CSS length, and what tokens.css has always carried).

md.$description: Medium radius. Mid-size controls and insets, a touch rounder than sm.

lg.$description: Large radius. The social links (--sbtn-radius) and other mid-weight containers.

xl.$description: Extra-large radius. The default for cards and modals (--card-radius), prominent panels and feature surfaces.

full.$description: Full round. Pills, tags, and circular buttons; forces a complete radius at any height.

hairline.$description: Default 1px hairline border; reads --color-border so it follows the theme. The standard card edge and divider.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Button borders moved out to the btn.* component tokens (Task 87).

strong.$description: Heavier 1px border; reads --color-border-strong. For edges that need to read past a hairline, such as interactive-card hover outlines.

me.natemills.usage.role: The 2px keyboard-focus outline composite.
me.natemills.usage.use: As the full focus-visible outline on interactive elements.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never delete it without providing a replacement focus style; it is the keyboard-focus indicator.

focus.$description: 2px focus outline; reads --color-focus-ring (ink on light, lime on dark). The keyboard-focus indicator, never removed without a replacement.

focus-ring-offset.$description: Offset between an element and its focus ring. Outsets the 2px ring so it clears the element edge.

base.$description: The narrow reading column, despite the base name. The standard page band is container.wide.

me.natemills.usage.role: The narrow reading column, despite the base name. The standard page band is container.wide.
me.natemills.usage.use: Capping line length inside a read-focused, single-column section. The skills section is the only one on it today.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Do not read base as the default container. The standard page band is container.wide, which nearly every section uses against this token's one. On a top-level section it also caps every direct child, so a new section quietly reads narrower and off-axis compared with the rest of the page, and no gate checks container width.
me.natemills.usage.decision: The name is historic and stays; the prohibition carries the meaning rather than a rename with 30-plus consumers.

wide.$description: Main content band. Stays proportional at 92vw (4% side gutters, matching the tablet/laptop feel) up to ~1826px viewport, then caps at 1680px so ultrawide layouts do not stretch without earning it (W38 ceiling kept, like the type and spacing scales). The old clamp(1440px,...) floor was removed: it froze the band at 1440px across the whole 1565-2181px range, so side margins ballooned to 240px on a 1920px screen (the 16-inch boxed-in bug, 2026-06-21).

bp.$description: Breakpoint reference values for documentation and audits only. CSS custom properties cannot be read inside media queries and no JS consumes these; the real breakpoints live in the media queries themselves, guarded by bp-lint.mjs.

touch-target-dot.$description: Carousel-dot hit area (WCAG 2.5.8 AA floor). Was consumed with an inline fallback but defined nowhere (audit TK-09).

logo-tile.$description: The square an organisation mark sits in on a content card: experience role logos, award marks, and Training credentials. Steps to logo-tile-lg from 768 up. Unified 2026-08-17 after a mobile review found Training rendering 52px credentials against 60px for the degree and 64px everywhere else, which read as three sizes with no rule.

logo-tile-lg.$description: The logo-tile square from 768 up, where cards have the width to carry a larger mark.

base.$description: Base stacking level. The default flow; nothing is lifted.

dropdown.$description: Dropdowns, popovers, and menus that open over page content.

sticky.$description: Sticky and fixed chrome: the site header and pinned bars.

overlay.$description: Scrims and floating chrome above the sticky layer (backdrops, the floating action button).

modal.$description: Modal dialogs and lightboxes sitting above their scrim.

tooltip.$description: Tooltips and hover hints above modals.

toast.$description: Toasts and the scroll-progress bar: the top-most transient chrome. Wide 100-unit gaps leave room to insert a layer without renumbering.

skip-link.$description: Skip-to-content link on focus: the top-most element of all, so keyboard users can always reach it over any chrome.

portrait-fade.$description: Legibility fade behind the testimonial portrait rail foot: transparent ink to near-solid ink so the name and role read over any photo. Single-consumer effect token on the precedent set by the retired brand-period shadow, minted in the W55 follow-up (2026-08-11) when literal alpha escapes were ruled out; the 0.92 endpoint lives here, not in a consumer file. Keeps a live var() so a brand-ink re-point propagates.

hero-light-warm.$description: Hero studio light: the warm key, Nathan's pick on 2026-09-23 (Warm key in the hero lights lab), which replaced the five lights and the dark-only backlight that ran before it. A tungsten pool up and to the left of the phones. The curve is a raised cosine, peak 0.62 falling as (0.5 + 0.5 cos(pi t)) to the power 1.35, sampled at 17 stops, so its slope eases to zero at both ends and no stop draws a ring of its own. On a dark ground CSS does not paint it: assets/hero-lights.js reads these stops off the element and redraws them in one dithered layer, because a gradient this faint on near-black is rounded to 8 bits and shows as rings (measured the same in Chromium, Chrome and WebKit). CSS still paints it on a light ground, where screen on white adds nothing, and whenever the redraw cannot run. The gel colour (255 196 132) has no token because the system has no warm-light scale; it is stated once, here. The alphas are light, not UI tint, so they sit off the --alpha-* ramp, the same ruling every hero light has carried.

hero-light-fill.$description: Hero studio light: the cool fill opposite the warm key, down and to the right of the phones, at about a third of its strength. Warm key against cool fill is what stops a lit scene reading as computed. Same curve family as --hero-light-warm (a raised cosine, here to the first power), same dithered redraw on dark and the same CSS fallback. The sky gel (140 178 240) is a light colour, not a UI colour, so the no-blue rule for interface colour does not reach it; it is stated once, here, off the --alpha-* ramp by the same ruling as the warm key.

100.$description: Feather: barely-there washes and the faintest fills. Absorbed the 0.02 to 0.05 cluster.

200.$description: Hairline: quiet dividers and borders, the --uth-divider weight. Absorbed 0.06, 0.07 and 0.1.

300.$description: Soft: the workhorse divider and tint step, the biggest cluster in the audit (17 uses at exactly 0.12). Absorbed 0.14 and 0.16.

400.$description: Medium: hover tints and strong dividers; the same weight as color.on-ink-hover. Absorbed 0.2 and 0.22.

500.$description: Strong: emphatic borders and mid washes. Absorbed the 0.26 to 0.4 cluster.

600.$description: Heavy: heavy tints, specimen bars and decorative poster ink. Absorbed the 0.45 to 0.66 cluster.

700.$description: Near-solid: the heaviest decorative veils and poster inks.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Near-solid: the heaviest decorative veils and poster inks (0.82 to 0.85 cluster). Added 2026-08-11, hours after the scale shipped, when Nathan ruled out literal escapes entirely; the first live proof the numbered scale inserts a step without renaming.

alpha.$description: Transparency, the alpha scale (W55, 2026-08-11). A PRIMITIVE: a sibling of the neutral and lime ramps, carrying no role of its own, which the semantic layer consumes. Every non-text alpha in the consumer files composes rgb(<base> / var(--alpha-N)) from these seven steps instead of a freehand value. Numbered like the colour primitives so a step stays insertable; the values are the natural clusters the 2026-08-11 audit measured (46 distinct freehand alphas collapsed to seven). Text never rides this ramp: readable text is solid by rule (design-system.md, accessibility section), and the on-ink, overlay, glass and shadow families keep their own tuned alphas by the same ruling.

glass.$description: Liquid-frosted header glass (.m-liquidfrostlit). Light defaults here; dark overrides under darkTheme + osDark. The #lg-dist refraction (feDisplacementMap scale 100) is JS-injected and gated to desktop + hover.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Frosted fill colour, painted as the panel’s padding-box layer. Near-white at 40% in light, ink at 50% in dark, so the bar tints whatever scrolls behind it toward the page substrate.

tint.$description: The frosted fill: tints whatever scrolls behind the panel toward the page colour.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Added 2026-09-13, both themes, at 0.7. Once the page scrolls, the bar sits over whatever the page is showing rather than over the hero, and the resting 0.4 let the Selected work photo wall through at 1.69:1 against a 3:1 floor. 0.7 is the measured floor for the pair it has to satisfy: at 0.55 the outline still reads 2.95:1, and above 0.7 the bar stops looking like glass for no further gain. Nathan picked it on 2026-09-13 from a five-by-five matrix of tint against ink. It rides with two ink moves that buy the headroom: the header nav one step darker in light, and the header button outline one step brighter in dark. Without those two, this same 0.7 fails and the bar has to go fully solid.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Do not raise this to buy contrast on its own. Tint and ink are separate levers and the ink ones are cheaper: pushing the tint alone to clear AA takes the bar all the way to opaque and kills the material.

tint-scrolled.$description: The frosted fill once the page has scrolled and the bar sits over content rather than the hero.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Tuned 2026-06-03 and tokenised in the W55 follow-up. Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: The stronger frosted tier for full-screen glass (the mobile nav drawer): a menu over a busy page needs readability over translucency, so it is far less see-through than glass.tint. Near-white at 90% in light, ink at 90% in dark; the dark flip rides the token, no per-selector override.

tint-strong.$description: The heavier frost, for full-screen glass like the mobile menu.

edge-top.$description: Top stop of the lit border gradient: a bright highlight along the top edge, as if light is catching the rim, giving the panel its 3D lift.

edge-bottom.$description: Bottom stop of the lit border gradient: near transparent, so the lit edge fades from top to bottom like a real bevel.

specular.$description: Inner top highlight, an inset box-shadow drawing the sharp specular line across the panel’s top edge. A transparent no-op in dark, where the tint alone reads.

me.natemills.usage.decision: The header carried this shadow until 2026-08-21, where it lifted a floating pill; removing it is deliberate. Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Drop shadow for glass that floats clear of the page: the ask-AI bar and the Under-the-Hood glass specimen. Tighter contact shadow plus soft ambient in dark. Not used on the site header, which is a full-bleed bar and deliberately casts no shadow.

shadow.$description: Drop shadow for glass that floats clear of the page.

blur.$description: Backdrop blur on the Chromium refraction path (desktop with a hover pointer), where it pairs with the #lg-dist displacement filter. 10px in light, 7px in dark.

blur-webkit.$description: Backdrop blur on the plain-frost fallback used everywhere without the displacement filter (Safari, iOS, mobile). 14px in light, 11px in dark.

saturate.$description: Backdrop saturation boost. Pumps the colour of whatever scrolls behind the bar so the frost reads as live glass, not a grey haze.

dim.$description: How far the header brightens what sits behind it at rest.

me.natemills.usage.decision: Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Backdrop brightness clamp at rest (1, no dimming). The Apple Liquid Glass trick: nudge the content behind the panel toward one substrate so nav text keeps AA contrast over anything. The scrolled value lives in glass.dim-scrolled.

Full authoring note, moved off the on-page table 2026-09-12: Backdrop brightness clamp once the page is scrolled past 120px and the header sits over content rather than the hero. Light brightens the content behind it so dark nav text stays legible; dark brightens it too, only slightly, so the near-white nav still reads over whatever scrolls behind (see darkTheme).

dim-scrolled.$description: How far the header brightens what sits behind it once the page scrolls.

color-dot-inactive.$description: The unfilled half of the carousel position indicator on dark: brighter grey to clear 3:1 on the near-black page.

me.natemills.usage.role: The header glass, once the page has scrolled off the hero, in dark theme only.
me.natemills.usage.decision: Added 2026-09-13 to close a measured WCAG failure. At rest the bar sits over the hero and the resting tint is fine; once scrolled it sits over whatever the page is showing, and the page shows bright things: the Kind words and footer gradient videos, the About showreel, and the Selected work photo mosaic. Composited through the resting ink at 0.5, the button outline measured 1.03:1 to 1.11:1 against 3:1, and the labels 2.98:1 to 3.20:1 against 4.5:1, in Chromium and in WebKit, in four different sections. Raising the ink to alpha-700 measured worst outline 3.36:1 and worst label 9.70:1 across a fourteen-stop sweep of the whole page, with no failure anywhere. Deliberately NOT a per-section rule: only two of the four offenders are the lime bands, and a roster of bright sections is a list that goes stale the next time a video or an image wall lands behind the bar.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Do not repoint this at the ink colour alone. The alpha is the whole mechanism: at full opacity the bar stops being glass, and below roughly alpha-600 the outline falls back under 3:1.

glass-tint-scrolled.$description: Dark: the scrolled bar carries its own ink so the page behind it stops deciding the header's contrast.

glass-specular.$description: Dark: no inner specular (transparent no-op so the box-shadow list stays valid). Tuned by Nathan 2026-06-04.

me.natemills.usage.role: Dark-theme value of the header-glass specular highlight: a deliberately transparent, zero-size inset shadow that holds the highlight's slot in the box-shadow list when dark mode wants no lit edge drawn.
me.natemills.usage.use: As the first shadow layer of the glass surfaces (the floating header pill, the ask-AI bar, the Under-the-Hood glass shards). Tune its colour or alpha if the dark rim should read; keep it a real shadow value either way.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never simplify it to none, however much it looks like a no-op. It is substituted into a comma-separated box-shadow list, where none is only legal as the WHOLE value, so the entire declaration falls back to none and the dark floating header silently loses its glass.shadow drop shadow too. Sibling darkTheme shadow tokens that are plain none are safe only because they are consumed alone.
me.natemills.usage.decision: The transparent zero-size form is load-bearing syntax, not a leftover.

glass-shadow.$description: Dark: tight contact shadow plus soft ambient. Tuned 2026-06-04.

glass-dim-scrolled.$description: Scrolled backdrop dim, dark: near-neutral per Nathan's 2026-06-04 tuning (was 0.4). NOTE: the old 0.4 darkened content behind the header to protect near-white nav contrast over light images; verify legibility over light content.

sbtn-gh-fg.$description: GitHub mark on dark: the brand black is invisible on a near-black page, so the mark goes monochrome and follows body text. Aliases the semantic layer rather than a primitive (audit M-19), so it tracks any change to dark text.

sbtn-li-fg.$description: LinkedIn mark on dark: the brand blue loses contrast on a near-black page, so the mark goes monochrome and follows body text. Aliases the semantic layer rather than a primitive (audit M-19), so it tracks any change to dark text.

highContrast.$description: prefers-contrast: more overrides layered on light. Authored here so the token source owns every theme path (audit TK-03); build.mjs emits the media query. Every value is an existing primitive.

highContrastDark.$description: prefers-contrast: more overrides layered on dark (explicit toggle AND OS dark; build.mjs emits both scopes from this one group).

gap.$description: Space between a social link's mark and its text stack.

stack-gap.$description: Space between the social link's eyebrow and its wordmark; 4px.

row-gap.$description: Space between social links in the hero row; 12px.

min-h-sm.$description: Hero social icon visual height on phones (max-width 768px). Now the SAME 44px as --sbtn-min-h: the phone treatment differs by SHAPE (a square, icon only, label clipped) not by size. Kept as its own name so the phone block reads as a deliberate treatment and can diverge again. At 44 the box is itself the 44px pointer target, so the ::after ghost is belt and braces rather than load bearing.

me.natemills.usage.role: Phone-only (max-width:768px) visual size for the hero social icons only.
me.natemills.usage.use: Width/height of .sbtn inside the max-width:768px scope, always paired with a 44px ghost hit area via ::after.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never below 768px as a general small-button size (that is btn.sm), never above 768px, and never let it fall under --touch-target-min: it IS the pointer target now.
me.natemills.usage.decision: 2026-09-06, Nathan: the phone treatment was 36px with the shared 14px radius, so the corner read as 39% of the box against 29% on tablet and the icons looked almost fully round, a different shape from the same component one breakpoint up. Measured on his phone, then reviewed as live toggles on the real page. The visual goes to the full 44px target (no ghost needed any more, the box IS the target) and the corner gets its own phone value so the PROPORTION matches tablet instead of the number matching. Verified: 44x44 icons, a 44x110 badge, and 22px of clearance still left between the row and the badge at 320px wide.

mark.$description: Social link logo height. Sized to the ink height of the two text lines (measured 27.3px, eyebrow cap top to wordmark descender), which no step on the --size-* scale matches.

mark-figma.$description: Figma mark height inside a social link. An optical correction, not a second size: Figma is the only portrait mark of the three (2:3), and a tower matched by height to the square [in] glyph and the round octocat beside it reads a size larger than both. 24px is six sevenths of --sbtn-mark and lands the three on the same optical weight.

mark-sm.$description: Social icon logo height inside the phone box. Now the same 28px as --sbtn-mark, because the phone box is the same 44px as the desktop one; the two stay separate names so the phone mark can diverge again without touching desktop.

mark-figma-sm.$description: Figma logo height inside the phone box. Now the same 24px as --sbtn-mark-figma, for the same reason as --sbtn-mark-sm. Figma's mark is taller than it is wide, so it sits below the square marks at every size.

gh-fg.$description: GitHub mark colour inside a social link. Theme-flipping: GitHub's near-black on a light plate, page ink on a dark one.

li-fg.$description: LinkedIn mark colour inside a social link, the boxless glyph used on mobile. Theme-flipping the same way as gh-fg: LinkedIn blue on a light plate, page ink on a dark one.

radius-sm.$description: Corner radius for the social links and the WCAG mark on phones (max-width 768px). Separate from --sbtn-radius because radius does not scale with a box on its own: the shared 14px sat on a 49px plate on tablet (29% of the height) and on a 44px square on phones (32%), and at the old 36px square it was 39% and read as a circle. 10px on the phone square restores the tablet PROPORTION. If either size moves, re-check the ratio rather than the number.

me.natemills.usage.role: Phone-only (max-width:768px) corner radius for .sbtn and .wcagm.
me.natemills.usage.use: border-radius on .sbtn and .wcagm inside the max-width:768px scope.
me.natemills.usage.doNotUse: Never above 768px (that is --sbtn-radius), never on a round control (those are --radius-full), never as a general small-card radius (that is --card-radius).
me.natemills.usage.decision: 2026-09-06, Nathan: the phone treatment was 36px with the shared 14px radius, so the corner read as 39% of the box against 29% on tablet and the icons looked almost fully round, a different shape from the same component one breakpoint up. Measured on his phone, then reviewed as live toggles on the real page. The visual goes to the full 44px target (no ghost needed any more, the box IS the target) and the corner gets its own phone value so the PROPORTION matches tablet instead of the number matching. Verified: 44x44 icons, a 44x110 badge, and 22px of clearance still left between the row and the badge at 320px wide.

mark.$description: W3C mark height inside the conformance badge. Sized to fill its cell; it stays under the text cell height so the badge keeps taking its overall height from the social link tokens. Raised from 36px to 43.2px on 2026-08-25 (Nathan, 20 percent): measured, the badge stays 49px tall and still matches the social links beside it, only its width grows by 7px.

mark-sm.$description: W3C mark height inside the phone badge. The whole wcagm.*-sm group scales the badge as ONE unit to the same height as the social icons beside it (44px since 2026-09-06, 36px before), keeping the exact desktop composition, mark cell + amber text cell, rather than simplifying it. Every driver has its own -sm value so the badge stays crisp text at every size instead of a blurry CSS zoom.

pad-y-sm.$description: WCAG badge text-cell block padding at the phone-only size; half of --sbtn-pad-y.

pad-x-sm.$description: WCAG badge inline padding (both cells) at the phone-only size; matches --space-2, two-thirds of --sbtn-pad-x.

stack-gap-sm.$description: Space between the social link's two text lines at the phone-only size; half of --sbtn-stack-gap. Under the space scale's own floor, so a raw literal like the other *-sm badge tokens.

label-size-sm.$description: WCAG badge "WCAG" line size at the phone-only size, down from --sbtn-label-size (16px): the smallest the bold wordmark can go and still read as a word rather than a texture.

eyebrow-size-sm.$description: WCAG badge "2.2 AA" line size at the phone-only size, down from --sbtn-eyebrow-size (11px).
